question: In May 2022, the Commission held a call for evidence on a recommendation on the prevention of harmful practices against women and girls, with adoption by the Commission planned for the fourth quarter of 2022. However, by the end of 2023, the recommendation had still not been published by the Commission. Given this: 1.
Why has the recommendation on the prevention of harmful practices against women and girls not been adopted and published by the Commission?
When will the Commission communicate about this recommendation?

Will the recommendation include the issues of ‘non-vital surgery and medical intervention on intersex infants and adolescents without their personal and fully informed consent (intersex genital mutilation), forced medicalisation of trans people and conversion practices targeting LGBTIQ people’, as mentioned in the LGBTIQ Equality Strategy 2020-2025?
answer: It is planned that the future Recommendation on harmful practices will be related to the directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence (1): both initiatives aim at preventing and combating gender-based violence.

The proposed directive sets legally binding minimum standards for the criminalisation of certain forms of gender-based violence, as well as for the prevention, protection, support and access to justice for victims of violence against women and domestic violence.

It is planned that the future Recommendation will identify concrete actions that Member States would be recommended to undertake to prevent and combat such practices most effectively on the ground. It is therefore intended to be partly complementary to the directive.

To ensure complementarity between the two instruments and be able to build on the measures agreed in the directive, the Commission opted to finalise the recommendation only after the adoption of the directive. Hence, the recommendation is planned for adoption in the course of 2024.

The content of the future Recommendation, including possible topics related to malpractices in the medical setting, is still under internal discussion. In the LGBTIQ Equality Strategy (2), the Commission committed to combat harmful practices such as the ones highlighted in the Honourable Member’s question, and fosters Member States’ exchange through the LGBTIQ Equality Subgroup.
Two discussions on legal gender recognition and on the ban on conversion practices took place at the Subgroup meetings of November 2022 and April 2023.
Proposal for a directive on combating violence against women and domestic violence, COM(2022)105 final. 8.3.2022. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52020DC0698
